newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends quiet day moderately weaker.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends quiet day moderately weaker.

text.p: CSCE cocoa prices ended moderately weaker Thursday, but managed to hold above nearby support levels, market sources said.

In what traders described as a relatively uneventful session, the market staged a short-lived bid to test the recent highs. But heavy industry-linked selling again emerged in the low 1,340s basis the May contract, leading to a flurry of speculative profit-taking.
Sellers retreated as May reached the $1,330 mark, leaving support intact at $1,325.
Most-active May futures fell $6 a tonne, to close at $1,330, having traded from $1,329 to $1,343. July futures also fell $6 a tonne, to $1,330, while the outer months eased between $4 and $8.
An estimated 3,919 lots were exchanged on the day, down sharply from Wednesday's official total of 11,217.
In other news, the director of Ivory Coast's marketing agency, Caistab, said the country endorses a policy of "production reduction".

Speaking to industry representatives at the Cocoa Merchants Association conference in Phoenix, Arizona, Caistab's Ives-Marie Koissy said seven years of over-production had led to sharply lower prices on the world market.

While he stressed that he is not in favor of adopting an export retention program like the one used by coffee producing countries, Koissy said the Ivory Coast would aim to keep production at around 900,000 tonnes per year. The Ivory Coast is the world's leading cocoa producer.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
